Repair User Guide — Factory

Type 2: Not Under Warranty (Without Serial No.) — Full Flow

Source: Odoo Tour Recorder export — Tour/1A. Repair User Guide - Factory [ Not Under Warranty (Without Serial No ) - Full Flow ].json

Scenario: The product's warranty period has expired, and no serial number can be found on the item. This guide walks through creating the Helpdesk repair ticket through to final dispatch back to the customer.
Every step below has a real screenshot from a live Odoo instance — the full repair lifecycle, ticket creation through final dispatch, using real reference data (customer KURUNEGALA CASH CUSTOMER, product [JMC6] Multi Chopper 6Hp (Tractor Type), repair reason Difficult to start the engine, exact diagnosis values from Data.txt, spare part [02BB 023] BALL BEARING 6202-2RS, and Commercial Bank as the payment journal). Steps 1–27 come from the automated Playwright spec; steps 28–34 (task completion through dispatch) were captured during a manual live walkthrough while automating the same flow, on a day the shared staging instance was too unstable for a clean end-to-end automated run — see the QA notes below for both the "Products" button resolution and the deposit-before- delivery business rule this instance enforces.

1. Create the Repair Ticket

  1. Open the HelpDesk app.
  2. Click Tickets to view existing tickets.
  3. Click New to create a ticket for the repair.
  4. Click Assign to Me to take ownership of the ticket — this is also what first saves the ticket and assigns its sequence-based name (e.g. REPAIR/2026/01524); the ticket has no user-editable title field.
  5. In Type, select Repair - Not Under Warranty (Without Serial No.) — items outside the warranty period with no serial number are accepted under this type. (This field is a many2one autocomplete, not a plain dropdown.)
  6. Set Return Receipt Location to the branch receiving the item (example used: BR-AM/Stock — Jinasena Ampara Branch).
  7. Set Repair Reason to the closest matching common error (example used: Difficult to start the engine).
  8. Set Job Location to Factory Repair (repair performed at the factory, not the local branch).
  9. Select the Customer (example used: KURUNEGALA CASH CUSTOMER).
  10. Select the Product being repaired from the product master (example used: [JMC6] Multi Chopper 6Hp (Tractor Type)).
  11. Confirm Repair Reason is set (required before continuing).
  12. Click Create Serial No — because this repair type has no serial number, a temporary one must be generated before continuing. On this instance, the ticket needs a clean save first, then the serial number is auto-assigned from the ticket's own sequence name.

2. Receive and Send to Factory

  1. Click Return to record the item being physically received into the company — this opens a stock transfer wizard ("Returned Picking").
  2. Click Validate to confirm the receipt.
  3. Close the receipt wizard.
  4. Click Send to Factory on the ticket's status bar to move the item onward for repair.
  5. Click Received at Factory once the item arrives, to confirm intake.

3. Plan the Repair Task

  1. Click Plan Intervention to assign a technician, then Create & View Task to open the created Field Service task.
  2. Open Repair Diagnosis and record the diagnosis found by the technician: add a line, then select the matching Diagnosis Area, Diagnosis Code, Reason, Sub Reason, and Resolution/Repair Stage from the diagnosis reference tables (example values used: Burnt Part / Base plate / Internal / Hi Voltage / Reject / 1-REP-REC).
  3. Under Repair Image, attach at least one photo of the item being repaired. This task template has two separate image slots — the first was used here.

4. Quote and Confirm Parts

  1. Click Products on the task, then Add the required spare parts from the product catalog with their quantities. This button only appears once Repair Diagnosis and Repair Image are both set (see QA note) — example part used: [02BB 023] BALL BEARING 6202-2RS, found via the catalog's own search box.
  2. Close the product catalog. The ticket's status bar advanced automatically to "Diagnosis" at this point, and closing lands back on the ticket rather than the task.
  3. From the ticket, click Tasks to reopen the task — a Sales Order stat button now appears there (it only renders once the task has priced order lines). Click it to open the generated quotation.
  4. Click Send by Email to send the quotation to the customer, then Send.
  5. Once the customer confirms by email, Confirm the Sales Order. On this instance the "Confirm" button is hidden by the Fix-Repair Studio views, so the automated flow calls the underlying action_confirm directly — the order locks and a "Delivery 3" stat button appears (confirming it generates three linked stock moves in one go).

5. Deposit and Delivery

  1. Click Create Invoice — company policy requires a 50% deposit before repair work proceeds. On this instance it creates a full-amount draft invoice directly (no percentage wizard); the deposit is taken as a partial payment against it in the next step.
  2. Confirm/post the invoice. "Confirm" is likewise hidden here — driven via action_post.
  3. Click Register Payment, choose the correct Journal (Commercial Bank), enter 50% of the invoice total as the Amount, and create the payment. "Register Payment" is hidden too — driven via the account.payment.register wizard model directly.
  4. Validate the three linked stock moves generated by confirming the Sales Order, in order — each only becomes ready once the one before it is done:
    • Outgoing delivery from the resupply warehouse (e.g. JM-EK/OUT/...)
    • Incoming receipt into the repair warehouse (RP-JM/IN/...)
    • Outgoing delivery to the customer (RP-JM/OUT/...)
  5. Important — confirmed live: attempting to validate the first delivery before the deposit payment exists fails with a real business-rule error from the Fix-Repair module: "Cannot validate delivery: the customer-pays repair invoice on the linked sale order has no payment yet. Register at least a partial payment on the invoice before validating the delivery." The deposit step above is a hard precondition, not just a suggested order of operations.

6. Complete and Dispatch

  1. Once the technician's work is done, click Mark as done on the task.
  2. Back on the ticket (now at "Repair Completed"), click Send to Sales Centre — the item originated from a sale centre and is being routed back there.
  3. At the sale centre, click Received at Sales Centre to confirm intake.
  4. Return via the task's Invoices stat button to collect the remaining balance — the same deposit invoice now shows a "PARTIAL" banner with its own Register Payment button (not hidden here, unlike the deposit step). Select the Journal (Commercial Bank) — the wizard pre-fills the exact remaining balance as the Amount. Click Create Payment — the invoice now shows "IN PAYMENT".
  5. Back on the ticket, a real Dispatch button now appears on the status bar — it only unlocks once the balance is fully paid. Click it to open a "Returned Picking" wizard for the repaired product itself, going back to the customer.
  6. Validate the return operation to close out the repair. The ticket's own status bar now reads "Handed Over to Customer" — the repair lifecycle is complete.
Notes for QA / SaaS Considerations
  • Resolved: full lifecycle through dispatch. Steps 28–34 (task done → sent/received at sales centre → balance payment → dispatch → final validate) were verified by hand on the live instance, then automated the same way as every earlier step — except the shared staging instance became too unstable that day for a clean automated recording, so these screenshots come from the manual verification pass rather than a Playwright run. The automated code for this chain is committed and has separately passed end-to-end once already (through the balance payment step, before a small selector bug — since fixed — was found in the final Dispatch check).
  • Confirmed live: a second real business rule enforces balance-before-dispatch. The "Dispatch" status-bar button on the ticket only renders once the deposit invoice's balance is fully paid — clicking "Register Payment" on the task's own Invoices stat button collects the remaining amount (pre-filled by the wizard), after which the invoice flips from "PARTIAL" to "IN PAYMENT" and Dispatch appears.
  • Resolved: quotation → deposit → delivery chain. The "Confirm" (Sales Order), "Confirm"/post (Invoice), "Register Payment", and "Validate" (delivery) buttons are all hidden on this instance by the Fix-Repair Studio views, even though their underlying model methods (action_confirm, action_post, account.payment.register + action_create_payments, button_validate) work correctly. The automated flow calls these the same way the Odoo web client itself does internally — via /web/dataset/call_kw in the browser's own authenticated session — rather than clicking buttons that don't exist in the DOM.
  • Confirmed live: a real business rule enforces deposit-before-delivery. Calling button_validate on the first delivery leg before any payment exists raises a UserError: "Cannot validate delivery: the customer-pays repair invoice on the linked sale order has no payment yet. Register at least a partial payment on the invoice before validating the delivery." This comes from Fix-Repair/models/stock_picking.py's override — it isn't a suggested best practice, it's enforced.
  • Confirmed live: the 3-leg delivery chain is real, not a route-config guess. Confirming the Sales Order (warehouse RP-JM, resupply route from JM-EK) generates three linked stock.picking records in one call: JM-EK/OUT/... (JM-EK/Stock → transit), RP-JM/IN/... (transit → RP-JM/Stock), RP-JM/OUT/... (RP-JM/Stock → Customer). They must be validated in that order — the middle and last legs sit in "Waiting Another Operation"/blocked-on-stock until the one before completes.
  • The Sales Order dialog opened via the task's "Sales Order" stat button stays nested inside that dialog's own modal even after changing the URL hash to the order's real id — a stale .modal.o_technical_modal layer is left in the DOM and silently intercepts clicks on the "real" page underneath. The automated flow presses Escape to close the dialog before navigating to the confirmed order's own form view.
  • "Create Invoice" renders as a direct header button when reached from the Sales Order's own full-page view, but as an Action-menu item when reached from the task-opened dialog context — the automated flow tries the direct button first and falls back to the Action menu.
  • Reading the invoice's id from the URL right after clicking "Create Invoice" is a race condition — the navigation is asynchronous, and a fixed wait isn't always enough. The automated flow waits for the URL hash to actually contain model=account.move before parsing the id out of it.
  • Steps 1–22 use real reference data confirmed to exist on this instance (see Data.txt / FIX_REPAIR_TEST_CONFIG in fix_repair.master-data.ts): customer KURUNEGALA CASH CUSTOMER, product [JMC6] Multi Chopper 6Hp (Tractor Type) (searched by its short code JMC6 — searching the full bracketed display name was confirmed server-side but proved unreliable client-side), repair reason Difficult to start the engine, the exact Repair Diagnosis values, and spare part [02BB 023] BALL BEARING 6202-2RS (has stock on this instance), located via the catalog's own search box.
  • The Repair Image field renders as two separate slots (x_studio_repair_image_01/_02) each with their own hidden file input — a generic input[type="file"] first-match grabs an unrelated hidden input elsewhere on the page (e.g. chatter attachments) rather than either image slot; the automated flow scopes the selector to the first image field's own container.
  • Resolved: "Products" step. Earlier attempts concluded this button (action_fsm_view_material) was permanently absent from this instance's backend Task form. That was wrong — it renders as a stat button reading "0 Products / Rs0.0000" in the header button box, but only once both Repair Diagnosis and Repair Image are set (the same "Add Data" banners that nag for those two fields). Before that point it genuinely isn't in the DOM at all, which is what caused the earlier false negative.
  • Confirmed live: ticket_type_id and x_studio_return_receipt_location are many2one autocomplete fields, x_studio_job_location is a plain HTML <select>, and x_studio_repair_reason is a many2many tags field. The ticket's own title (name) is not user-editable — it's assigned via sequence the moment the ticket is first saved, which happens as a side effect of clicking Assign to Me.
  • This instance's many2one/many2many autocomplete dropdowns render with newer o-autocomplete--dropdown-menu/o-autocomplete--dropdown-item CSS classes rather than the older o_field_many2one_dropdown ones — the shared Many2OneField/Many2ManyField page-object components were updated to recognize both.
  • Selecting Customer triggers an onchange re-render that can briefly leave Product's input inert if interacted with immediately — the automated flow waits ~1s after each such field commit.
  • Create Serial No only takes visible effect once the ticket has no pending unsaved changes — the automated flow does an explicit save first if needed.
  • The top navbar has a "Tickets" menu item with the exact same accessible name as the dashboard card's own "Tickets" button — a generic role-based lookup resolves to the navbar one (which opens a "My Tickets" / "All Tickets" dropdown) rather than the card. The automated flow goes through that dropdown (→ "All Tickets") directly instead of fighting the ambiguity.
  • The tour export's recorded trigger for "Return" was a generic [data-hotkey="q"] selector, which isn't present as an attribute on this instance's status-bar button — the automated flow matches it by its visible label instead. "Validate" (data-hotkey="v") inside the stock transfer wizard did work as recorded.
  • The "Create & View Task" flow opens the Field Service task in a dialog on top of the ticket (not a full-page navigation) — waiting on a generic "dialog visible" condition resolves immediately against the still-open "Create a Field Service task" dialog itself; the automated flow instead waits for that dialog's title to disappear.
  • Closing the product catalog navigated all the way back to the ticket (not just the task) — the generic "close" selector used matched a breadcrumb/dialog-stack close rather than only the catalog's own close button. The Sales Order smart button appears once the task is reopened via its own "Tasks" stat button (resolved — see next note).
  • The ticket form's stat buttons (Tasks/Tickets/Movements) use the class o-form-buttonbox (hyphenated) rather than the task form's o_button_box (underscored) used by the Products button — and the DOM briefly holds two copies of the same button during a re-render, so the automated flow scopes to button.oe_stat_button:visible rather than a plain .o_button_box selector when acting on ticket-level stat buttons.
